How it works

1 · Model
Named parameters in Inventor: thickness, slot, small-end wall.
2 · Simulate
The study is started by hand, because Inventor’s solver can’t be scripted.
3 · Read
Python reads the exported report and rejects results that don’t match the model.
4 · Decide
The AI proposes the next change and the cycle repeats.

Study setup

Material
Steel, yield strength 207.0 MPa.
Load
Bearing load of 10000 N, component along Y: -10000 N.
Support
Pin constraint, fixed in the radial, axial, tangential direction(s).
Study
Rod_10kN_compression: linear static analysis, mesh refined until the change fell below the stop criterion.

Engineering notes

1 · The rod swung free
With the big end left free to turn, the solver warned of large deformation and the rod carried almost no stress. Fixing all three directions of the pin removed it.
2 · Unstable peak
Peak stress moved between 72 and 82 MPa from run to run, because the mesh refined in different places. The peak sits where the thick small end meets the thinner neck.
3 · Fillets
A 2 mm fillet on both faces of that corner, with refinement over the whole part, settled the baseline.
4 · Thicker shank
A thicker shank lowered the peak stress and lifted the safety factor above the target.

Toolchain

Autodesk Inventor Professional 2026 · Python (pywin32) · an MCP server · Claude

get_parameters
Lists the model’s driving and read-only dimensions and its mass.
set_parameter
Changes one allowed dimension, rebuilds the part and restores it if the rebuild fails.
parse_latest_report
Reads stress, displacement, safety factor and mass, and flags a report that doesn’t match the model.
save_run · generate_report
Stores each run with its plots and builds the final HTML report.

Limits

One load case and a fully fixed support, which is stiffer than a real pin. No buckling, fatigue or tension case, and the bolts are not modelled. Peak stress at a local corner depends on the mesh and the fillet size.
